deck.title: Storage Gateway, DataSync & Transfer Family
deck.analogy: Storage Gateway is a magic filing cabinet in your office whose drawers extend to an S3 warehouse; DataSync is a moving company; Transfer Family is a staffed loading dock for SFTP partners.

subtopics.title: Storage Gateway — the ongoing hybrid bridge
Transfer Family — the managed SFTP dock

cards.front: What problem do Storage Gateway, DataSync and Transfer Family solve together?

back.answer: Hybrid storage: on-prem servers speak NFS/SMB/iSCSI/tape, while cheap infinite storage lives in AWS (S3).
back.explanation: Servers can't be rewritten overnight, so cloud storage must look local to them.
back.mnemonic: Office filing room vs. infinite warehouse across town (S3).

cards.front: What is AWS Storage Gateway in the analogy, and is it temporary?

back.answer: A magic filing cabinet in your office with a local cache; an ONGOING bridge that stays forever.
back.explanation: Hot folders stay in the drawer (local cache); everything else lives in the cloud.

cards.front: What are DataSync and Transfer Family in the analogy?

back.answer: DataSync is a professional moving company (migration); Transfer Family is a staffed loading dock for SFTP partners.
back.explanation: DataSync moves files with labels and permissions intact, then leaves; Transfer Family lets partners keep delivering via SFTP straight into S3.
back.mnemonic: Moving company vs. staffed loading dock.

cards.front: How is Storage Gateway deployed, and what gives low-latency access to hot data?

back.answer: As a VM or hardware appliance on-premises, backed by cloud storage, with a local cache.
back.explanation: The cache keeps frequently used data local.

cards.sourceHeading: Storage Gateway — the ongoing hybrid bridge

cards.front: Storage Gateway: S3 File Gateway — protocol, backing store, exam phrase?

back.answer: NFS/SMB, backed by S3 (real objects); "Replace the NAS; files in S3; keep local file access."

cards.sourceHeading: Storage Gateway — the ongoing hybrid bridge

cards.front: Storage Gateway: FSx File Gateway — protocol, backing store, exam phrase?

back.answer: SMB, backed by FSx for Windows; low-latency on-prem access to FSx Windows shares.

cards.sourceHeading: Storage Gateway — the ongoing hybrid bridge

cards.front: Storage Gateway: Volume Gateway Cached — protocol, where is primary data, exam phrase?

back.answer: iSCSI; primary data in S3, hot cache local; "Expand on-prem storage capacity."
back.explanation: The disk is bigger than your building.

cards.sourceHeading: Storage Gateway — the ongoing hybrid bridge

cards.front: Storage Gateway: Volume Gateway Stored — protocol, where is primary data, exam phrase?

back.answer: iSCSI; primary data LOCAL with async snapshots to S3; "low-latency access to the ENTIRE dataset" plus backup/DR.

cards.sourceHeading: Storage Gateway — the ongoing hybrid bridge

cards.front: Storage Gateway: Tape Gateway — protocol, backing store, exam phrase?

back.answer: iSCSI VTL, backed by S3 then Glacier; "Replace physical tape backup infrastructure."

cards.sourceHeading: Storage Gateway — the ongoing hybrid bridge

cards.front: Storage Gateway Volume Gateway: Cached vs Stored — which holds all data where?

back.answer: Cached: all data in S3, hot cache local (capacity). Stored: all data local, async snapshots to S3 (speed + DR).

cards.sourceHeading: Storage Gateway — the ongoing hybrid bridge

cards.front: Trap: Storage Gateway needs low-latency access to the FULL dataset — Cached or Stored?

back.answer: Stored — a cache only keeps the hot slice, so everything must live locally.
back.explanation: Cached is for capacity expansion, not full-dataset low latency.

cards.sourceHeading: Storage Gateway — the ongoing hybrid bridge

cards.front: Why does Storage Gateway Tape Gateway work with existing backup software like Veeam or NetBackup?

back.answer: It presents a Virtual Tape Library (VTL), so the software sees tapes while data lands in S3 and Glacier.
back.explanation: Any scenario with the word "tape" ends at Tape Gateway.

cards.sourceHeading: Storage Gateway — the ongoing hybrid bridge

cards.front: What is AWS DataSync and what are its sources and destinations?

back.answer: A migration/scheduled-transfer engine: one-time or scheduled sync from on-prem NFS/SMB into S3, EFS, or FSx.
back.explanation: Uses an on-prem agent and is built for TB-scale transfers.

cards.front: What DataSync features protect metadata and office bandwidth?

back.answer: It preserves file metadata and permissions, and supports bandwidth throttling.

cards.front: Can DataSync move data between AWS storage services, and is an agent needed?

back.answer: Yes — S3 ↔ EFS ↔ FSx, with no agent needed.

cards.front: DataSync vs Storage Gateway: what is the core distinction?

back.answer: DataSync MOVES data (one-time/scheduled); Storage Gateway gives ongoing hybrid ACCESS.
back.explanation: The truck leaves vs. the bridge stays.

cards.front: Trap: migrate 50 TB from on-prem NAS to S3 preserving permissions — S3 File Gateway or DataSync?

back.answer: DataSync — a gateway is for continuing access, not bulk moves.
back.explanation: Flip side: keeping on-prem apps using files that must live in S3 means a gateway.

cards.front: What is AWS Transfer Family?

back.answer: A fully managed SFTP/FTPS/FTP endpoint in front of S3 or EFS.
back.explanation: Partners keep their SFTP workflows; files land directly in your bucket.

cards.sourceHeading: Transfer Family — the managed SFTP dock

cards.front: Trap: partners upload via SFTP — should you run an SFTP server on EC2?

back.answer: No — use Transfer Family; an EC2 SFTP server is undifferentiated heavy lifting.

cards.sourceHeading: Transfer Family — the managed SFTP dock

cards.front: When does the scenario point beyond DataSync/Storage Gateway to the Snow Family?

back.answer: When offline, or data is so huge the network math fails (weeks of transfer, remote sites, limited bandwidth).
back.explanation: Covered in Section 27.

cards.front: A company wants to eliminate physical tape backup infrastructure but keep its existing backup software. Which service?

back.answer: Tape Gateway
back.explanation: VTL to S3/Glacier; software sees tapes.

cards.front: Replace an aging NAS; store files in S3 but keep low-latency local access over SMB/NFS. Which?

back.answer: S3 File Gateway
back.explanation: Cloud-backed share with local cache.

choices.why: Moves data; no ongoing local access.
NFS/SMB share backed by S3 with cache.

cards.front: Migrate 50 TB from an on-prem NAS to S3, preserving permissions and metadata, minimal effort. Which?

back.answer: DataSync
back.explanation: Migration engine preserving metadata.

choices.why: For ongoing access, not bulk moves.
Built for migration with metadata preserved.

cards.front: Business partners upload files via SFTP, can't change workflow; files must land in S3. Which?

back.answer: Transfer Family
back.explanation: Managed SFTP endpoint.

cards.front: On-prem app needs low-latency access to the ENTIRE dataset, with backups to AWS for DR. Which?

back.answer: Volume Gateway — Stored
back.explanation: Full data local, async snapshots to S3.

choices.why: Entire dataset local plus S3 snapshots.

cards.front: On-prem storage is running out of space; extend capacity while keeping frequently used data fast. Which?

back.answer: Volume Gateway — Cached
back.explanation: Primary in S3, hot cache local.

choices.why: Cloud primary, hot data cached locally.

cards.front: Copy files nightly from on-prem SMB shares to EFS, with bandwidth throttling. Which?

back.answer: DataSync
back.explanation: Scheduled transfers and throttling are signature features.

choices.why: Targets S3, not EFS scheduled copies.
Scheduled sync to EFS with throttling.

cards.front: Low-latency on-prem access to file shares stored on FSx for Windows File Server. Which?

back.answer: FSx File Gateway

choices.why: SMB cache for FSx Windows shares.

cards.front: Transfer data between S3 and EFS within AWS. Which?

back.answer: DataSync
back.explanation: Works AWS-to-AWS, agentless.

choices.why: SFTP front end, not AWS-to-AWS sync.
Agentless transfers among S3, EFS, FSx.

cards.front: Keyword: **"Replace tape backups"**

back.answer: Tape Gateway (VTL → S3/Glacier)

cards.front: Keyword: **"NAS replacement, files in S3, local access"**

back.answer: S3 File Gateway

cards.front: Keyword: **"SMB cache for FSx Windows"**

back.answer: FSx File Gateway

cards.front: Keyword: **"Extend on-prem capacity, primary in cloud"**

back.answer: Volume Gateway — Cached

cards.front: Keyword: **"Full dataset local + snapshots to cloud"**

back.answer: Volume Gateway — Stored

cards.front: Keyword: **"Migrate / scheduled sync, preserve permissions"**

back.answer: DataSync

cards.front: Keyword: **"Bandwidth throttling, on-prem agent"**

back.answer: DataSync

cards.front: Keyword: **"S3 ↔ EFS ↔ FSx transfers"**

back.answer: DataSync

cards.front: Keyword: **"Partners upload via SFTP/FTPS/FTP"**

back.answer: Transfer Family (never SFTP-on-EC2)

cards.front: Keyword: **"Ongoing hybrid access vs. one-time move"**

back.answer: Storage Gateway vs. DataSync

cards.front: Keyword: **"Offline / massive data, no bandwidth"**

back.answer: Snow Family (Section 27)
